title: P2 · His summary is assembled and signed
description: Onesa's HIE assembles Kamal's International Patient Summary from his care history: his conditions, his medicines, his allergy. It issues a Verifiable Health Link to it, signs it with a key registered with GDHCN, and puts the QR code in his wallet. Step 2 of the overview of key process flows.

illustrationStyle.prompt: Warm, flat digital illustration with soft shading and clean outlines, friendly and respectful, in the style of a public-health storybook. Wide banner, aspect ratio 11:4. Bright natural daylight, soft pastel palette with clear colour accents. Faces in gentle three-quarter view with expressive, kind features. Technology shown as simple, oversized icons: a phone with a QR code, a shield with a check mark, a small speech bubble with a symbol. No readable text, no logos, no real brands, no flags with text. All people are fictional.

cast.description: Onesan man, 61, slim, short grey hair, kind face. Batik shirt in Onesa. In Taifafeki, white two-piece ihram (unstitched towelling cloth, right shoulder bare when in ihram), a small waist pouch and one phone.

notes: Ihram (two white unstitched sheets) is for men only; women wear ordinary modest clothing, usually white, face and hands uncovered.
Keep the Kaaba and other holy sites far in the background or out of frame.
Keep medical signs text-free so generators don't invent wrong Arabic.
The picture carries no text: the step title and the caption are page text.

steps.title: His summary is assembled and signed
steps.headline: Onesa's HIE turns Kamal's care history into a signed patient summary and puts the link to it in his wallet as a QR code.
steps.narrative: Onesa's HIE assembles Kamal's International Patient Summary from his care history: his conditions, his medicines, his allergy. It issues a Verifiable Health Link to it, signs it with a key registered with GDHCN, and puts the QR code in his wallet. Step 2 of the overview of key process flows.

experiences.doing: Assembles the IPS (conditions, medicines, allergy), issues a Verifiable Health Link to it, and signs it with a key registered with GDHCN.
Receives the QR code and keeps it ready to show.
Sees the QR code appear in his wallet as he packs.
experiences.feeling: “Everything they need is in my phone.”

steps.painPoint: Without a signed summary, a clinic abroad has only what Kamal can remember and explain.
steps.enabler: One signed link, issued at home, that any participating country can verify.
steps.policy: What must the summary contain for a pilgrim — and who decides what is left out?

handoff.summary: The VHL QR code is in Kamal's wallet
handoff.payload: Signed VHL (QR code) to the IPS

illustration.alt: Icons for his conditions, medicines and allergy are gathered into one summary, stamped with a green shield by a golden key and turned into a QR code on the phone Kamal holds beside his packed suitcase.
illustration.prompt: A stylised server room merging into a document. Soft-glowing panels assemble a one-page patient summary from three icons: a heart (conditions), a pill bottle and insulin pen (medicines), and a red allergy warning symbol. A golden key stamps a shield with a check mark onto it. On the right the summary shrinks into a QR code and flies into a phone in Kamal's hand; he stands at home in batik with a packed suitcase. No readable text.

record.description: His IPS is signed and its QR code is in his wallet
